evals.prompt: Define component architecture for a reusable UI library in 2-3 sentences. Include layer, API surface, state contract, and theming separation.
expected_elements: Defines the subject as structuring reusable UI components across products, themes, or teams
Mentions primitives, composites, and product-specific assemblies
Mentions API surface such as props, slots, events, refs, render functions, or compound parts
Mentions controlled, uncontrolled, or hybrid state contracts
Mentions headless/styled or behavior/presentation separation

evals.prompt: Explain the mental model of component architecture. Name at least 8 primitives and how they connect.
expected_elements: At least 8 of: primitive, composite, product assembly, prop, slot, compound part, callback, render prop, ref, imperative handle, controlled value, default value, token binding, headless behavior, styled wrapper
Explains dependency direction from assemblies to composites to primitives
Explains API surface as public contract
Explains state contract as consumer-owned, component-owned, or hybrid
Explains theming separation as behavior and visual treatment evolving independently
absent_signals: Must not confuse component architecture with app-wide state management

evals.prompt: Why does this skill exist for agents working in component-heavy codebases? Name the failure modes it prevents.
expected_elements: Prevents treating a design system as a flat pile of widgets
Prevents primitives from depending on product-specific assemblies
Prevents visual language being hardcoded into reusable behavior
Prevents uncontrolled API growth through many independent props
Prevents implicit state ownership that breaks consumers
Prevents accessibility being retrofitted outside the primitive layer

evals.prompt: Distinguish component architecture from design-module-composition, design-system-architecture, color-system-design, form-ux-architecture, state-management, and a11y. Give a mechanism-level reason each neighbor differs.
expected_elements: design-module-composition wires a single product's modules or regions
design-system-architecture owns tokens, governance, documentation, distribution, and system meta-structure
color-system-design owns palette, contrast, semantic color, and color tokens
form-ux-architecture owns validation, submission, grouping, and error experience
state-management owns state location across app/client/server/URL/persistence
a11y audits accessibility behavior and conformance
component architecture owns reusable component layers, API surface, state contracts, and behavior/presentation split
absent_signals: Must not claim component-architecture owns token or governance decisions

evals.prompt: Classify a Button, Dialog, FormField, DataTable, SettingsPanel, and CheckoutForm into primitive, composite, or product-specific assembly. Explain dependency direction.
expected_elements: Button and Dialog primitive/root parts can be primitives when they provide base behavior
FormField and DataTable are usually composites
SettingsPanel and CheckoutForm are product-specific assemblies
Dependencies flow from assemblies to composites to primitives
Primitives must not import product-specific assemblies or visual decisions that prevent reuse
Mentions that some components can shift layer based on responsibility and reuse scope
absent_signals: Must not classify CheckoutForm or other product assemblies as a primitive

evals.prompt: Give an analogy for component architecture that preserves API contract, dependency direction, and behavior/presentation separation. Then name one bad analogy.
expected_elements: Uses API design, building-system, or layered-platform analogy
Maps component props/slots/events to public contract
Maps dependency direction to lower-level parts supporting higher-level assemblies
Maps headless/styled split to stable behavior versus replaceable presentation
Rejects a bad analogy that treats components as a grab bag or image catalog

evals.prompt: Novel scenario: A reusable SearchBox component has 18 mostly independent props, hardcoded brand colors, internal-only value state, and product-specific analytics. Diagnose the component architecture problems and propose a repair path.
expected_elements: Flags prop explosion and considers composition, slots, or compound parts
Moves hardcoded brand colors to styled layer or tokens
Makes state contract explicit as controlled, uncontrolled, or hybrid
Separates product-specific analytics into assembly/adapters/callbacks
Preserves accessibility in primitive behavior
Explains migration/deprecation for changed API
absent_signals: Must not recommend adding boolean props for structural variations

evals.prompt: Correct this statement: 'A design system is just a folder of components; if a component needs flexibility, add another prop.'
expected_elements: Corrects design system as tokens/foundations/components/distribution/governance rather than a component pile
Explains component architecture as primitives/composites/assemblies with dependency direction
Warns against independent prop multiplication
Recommends composition, slots, compound components, or render functions for open variation
Requires explicit API and state contracts
absent_signals: Must not state that a flat pile of components constitutes a design system
